day_shape: 75 items: Iran-Oman Hormuz talks dominate with Araghchi-Tajani call and JPost reporting on registration requirement, IDF resumes southern Lebanon strikes after Hezbollah ceasefire-violation warning, Netanyahu rejects early Gaza pullback, UN says Iran executed 56 since March.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz transit regime negotiations
threads.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said Iran-Oman talks on a safe Hormuz transit route have run for two months, and Araghchi briefed Italian FM Tajani by phone on the process. Jerusalem Post reported diplomatic sources saying ships would need to coordinate with Iran even when exiting via Oman, while Defa Press cited a Telegraph report on Europe potentially paying transit costs.

threads.label: Hormuz closure economic knock-on effects
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported many Iraqi public employees have not received July salaries owing to the prolonged Hormuz export disruption. Iran International reported an Iranian state bank froze National Iranian Oil Company accounts over debt, and detailed record inflation debate inside Iran.

threads.label: IDF resumes southern Lebanon strikes
threads.summary: The IDF issued evacuation warnings for Mansouri, Arnaya, Anqoun and Kafr Fila and began what it called precise strikes against Hezbollah, the first such evacuation warning since June. Lebanese state media reported one dead and 11 wounded from a strike on a prayer room in Tebnine; IDF also publicised dismantling of a Hezbollah tunnel in Srebbine.

threads.label: Netanyahu rejects early Gaza pullback
threads.summary: Netanyahu said the IDF will not withdraw from current lines in Gaza until Hamas is fully disarmed, in apparent opposition to a US-backed Board of Peace plan for an initial pullback. Defa Press cited Gaza Health Ministry figures of 73,381 killed and 174,231 injured since October 2023, and IDF publicised a rocket-filled tunnel demolition in southern Gaza.

threads.label: Al-Aqsa and Arab-Islamic ministerial response
threads.summary: Defa Press and IRIB reported Jordan convened an emergency meeting of Arab and Islamic foreign ministers over what it called an imminent threat of Al-Aqsa seizure, citing over 2,000 settler entries into the compound. Defa Press said the joint statement agreed a permanent mechanism to document Israeli violations at Jerusalem holy sites.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressures and human rights
threads.summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk said Iran has executed at least 56 people on national security charges since 19 March, including 27 linked to earlier protests. Iran International also reported nurses detained after a Tehran hospital strike, and described parliament as fading from power with authority shifting to the IRGC.

threads.label: Red Sea and Yemen maritime activity
threads.summary: UKMTO reported an incident 9 nautical miles southwest of Mokha involving an unmanned surface vessel attack that caused a fire aboard a ship, according to Defa Press. Defa Press also relayed a Yemeni foreign ministry warning to Riyadh of "comprehensive escalation" if tensions intensify.

events.summary_en: Iranian official: Entry and exit of ships in the Strait of Hormuz must be registered in a special system. Al-Mayadeen network reported from an Iranian security-political source that negotiations between Iran and Oman on joint arrangements for managing the Strait of Hormuz have reached important stages. The source added that Iran emphasises that one of the necessary arrangements is the registration of any entry or exit through the Strait of Hormuz in a special system. He told Al-Mayadeen that Iran believes this measure enables Tehran to exercise complete oversight of shipping and helps prevent incidents in the Strait of Hormuz. This Iranian official stressed that Oman continues to conduct consultations and negotiations.

events.title_en: SpaceX rocket collides with the Moon
events.summary_en: SpaceX rocket collides with the Moon. A piece of an American space rocket, after wandering in space for 19 months, collided with the lunar surface. This section of SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket was expected to burn up upon re-entry into Earth's atmosphere or fall into the ocean, but SpaceX was unable to place it in a safe orbit, as a result it was on a collision course with the Moon. The Falcon 9 rocket in its previous year's mission had transported two landers toward the Moon. This section of the rocket, which had been abandoned in space, weighed approximately four tonnes and was the size of a school bus, and scientists say that after colliding with the Moon's sphere it left a crater approximately four metres deep on the surface of this celestial body.
